key_insight: The paper compares direct and indirect PINN formulations for Dirichlet boundary control of semilinear parabolic PDEs and provides a conditional error analysis for the indirect approach.
engineering_relevance: This work supports more reliable PINN-based optimal control solvers for PDE-constrained engineering problems with boundary actuation and Tikhonov regularization.
method: Direct PINN: separate state and control networks minimize a penalized tracking objective.
Indirect PINN: state, adjoint, and control networks are trained jointly to satisfy the first-order optimality system.
Error analysis for the indirect method splits total error into approximation, optimization, quadrature, and soft-constraint terms.
evidence_signal: The authors validate the formulations on two manufactured test problems: a cubic reaction-diffusion equation and a linear case with nontrivial boundary control and adjoint.
watch_item: The reliability bound is conditional on regularity, local neighborhood assumptions, and soft constraint residual control, so performance may degrade if these assumptions are not met in practice.
paper_title: Direct and Indirect Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Dirichlet Boundary Control of Semilinear Parabolic Equations: A Conditional Error Analysis
